bypass_analysis.note: a difference or mask confined to the bypass bits crosses 1 round(s) without activating any S-box and must then enter an S-box, because the permutation sends both bypass bits onto S-box bits; single free rounds can still recur, which is what lowers the multi-round active-S-box bound

caveats: The active-S-box counts are a LOWER BOUND from a branch-number relaxation that models only which bits each S-box reads and writes, the branch number, and the bit permutation.

The probability and correlation figures bound a SINGLE CHARACTERISTIC under the independent-round heuristic; they are not differential-hull or linear-hull bounds and not a proof of resistance to differential or linear cryptanalysis.
No related-key, boomerang, integral, algebraic or meet-in-the-middle analysis is performed, and the key schedule is not modelled.
A trail attaining the bound need not exist: the model ignores whether the required single-bit DDT/LAT transitions are possible.

statements: Every S-box of the family has differential and linear branch number 2, the smallest possible value, so a single active bit can remain a single active bit from round to round. Unlike PRESENT, whose S-box has differential branch number 3, this cipher gets no help from its S-box in the wide-trail argument.
State bits 1 and 0 bypass the S-layer, so a trail can cross rounds without activating any S-box, which is why the 16-round bound stays well below 16 active S-boxes.
The branch-number bound alone therefore does NOT reach the 2**-32 data limit at 16 rounds for the DAC or the E-DAC S-box: it knows nothing about which DDT/LAT transitions exist.

The exact search with the real DDT and LAT is sharper: the MILP bound is attained by DAC-OPT in both models but not by DAC or E-DAC, and the best single characteristic of every S-box of the family crosses the data limit within the 16 rounds. On the differential side the APN tables are the last to get there, because their single-bit transitions chain through the bit permutation: S-box optimality does not transfer to the cipher.

linear_mask_permutation.derivation: (L^T)^{-1} over GF(2), L the matrix of the bit permutation

round_function.bit_index_convention: MSB-first index i denotes state bit 31 - i (index 0 = most significant state bit)
round_function.bypass_operation: complement (state ^= 0x3); affine, hence transparent to differences and to linear masks
round_function.perm_rule: the bit at MSB-first index i moves to MSB-first index PERM_TABLE[i]
round_function.text:
State: 32 bits b31..b0 (b31 = most significant). MSB-first index i denotes state bit 31 - i. Key: 80 bits. Rounds: 16.
Round r = 0..15: state ^= RK[r]; state = S-layer(state); state = P-layer(state), except in the last round (r = 15) where the P-layer is skipped; after the last round state ^= RK[16].
S-layer: six parallel copies of the same bijective 5-bit S-box, S0 on state bits 31..27; S1 on state bits 26..22; S2 on state bits 21..17; S3 on state bits 16..12; S4 on state bits 11..7; S5 on state bits 6..2. Each S-box writes its 5-bit output back to the five state bits it read, the more significant state bit of a window carrying the more significant bit of the S-box input and of its output. State bits 1 and 0 (MSB-first indices 30 and 31) enter no S-box: the layer replaces them by their complements (state ^= 0x3).
P-layer: the bit at MSB-first index i moves to MSB-first index PERM_TABLE[i], i.e. state bit 31 - i moves to state bit 31 - PERM_TABLE[i], with PERM_TABLE = [0, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 4, 10, 16, 22, 28, 2, 8, 14, 20, 26, 1, 7, 13, 19, 25, 31, 5, 11, 17, 23, 29, 3, 9, 15, 21, 27].
Key schedule: an 80-bit register K holds the master key; for i = 0..16: RK[i] = K >> 48; then K = rotate_left_80(K, 13); the top five bits of K are replaced by S(K >> 75); K ^= ((i + 1) mod 32) << 15.
Both the key addition and the complement of state bits 1 and 0 are affine, so neither changes a difference or a linear mask: only the six S-boxes and the bit permutation matter for the analysis below.
